samples.summary: Docs `FormatPainterToggle` re-implements the shipped slides `FormatPainterButton` (same `IconBrush`, `Toggle size="sm"`, `aria-label="Format painter"`, same `useEffect` mirror of an editor-side `has*/on*Change` pair) as a private component in the docs toolbar, rather than extracting a shared toolbar control the way the repo does for other cross-app toolbar pieces (`@/components/text-formatting/*`, used by both docs and slides). The task doc itself says the toggle should be "modelled on the shipped slides `FormatPainterButton`" (docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-surface-existing-features-todo.md:44). The two engine APIs genuinely differ (paint-mode vs copy/paste buffer), so this is reuse that was available but not strictly required — cost stays inside the codebase (two near-identical toggles that can drift in icon/label/pressed-state semantics).
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/format-painter.tsx:31-64 vs the new FormatPainterToggle in docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx

samples.summary: The dialog re-derives the effective page box inline (`orientation === "landscape" ? paperSize.height : paperSize.width`) instead of using `getEffectiveDimensions(setup)`, which is exported from `@wafflebase/docs` (packages/docs/src/index.ts:46) precisely for this and is what the engine, CLI and PDF exporter all use. A second copy of the orientation-swap rule in the frontend is exactly the kind of duplication the engine helper exists to prevent; if the model ever changes how orientation maps to dimensions, the dialog's validation silently disagrees with pagination.

The pagination design doc now contradicts itself: the Non-Goals list still carries "Page setup UI (modal dialog, side panel)" as a non-goal while annotating that it has shipped. The repo files docs by validity — a shipped capability belongs in the body (which the new "Page setup UI" section is), not left standing in Non-Goals with a retraction. Cost is documentation clarity only.
samples.evidence: "- Page setup UI (modal dialog, side panel) — was deferred to frontend integration; it has since shipped, see [Page setup UI](#page-setup-ui)."

samples.summary: Markdown/plain-text download silently drops the document header and footer (`includeHeaderFooter` left at its `false` default), while the DOCX and PDF exports of the same document include them. The comment justifies it by the CLI's terminal-stream rationale, but a downloaded file is the user's copy of the document, so the two export families now answer "what is in my document?" differently. Worth a deliberate decision (and a line in a design doc) rather than inheriting the CLI default.

In a read-only doc the Page Setup dialog and the format-painter toggle are rendered fully enabled, but the engine neuters `setPageSetup` (added to `MUTATING_METHODS`) and `pasteFormat` returns `false`, so "Apply" closes the dialog having written nothing and the painter's second press paints nothing — with no user-visible feedback. This mirrors the toolbar's pre-existing treatment of other mutating controls, so it is consistency with an existing gap rather than a new class of problem, but the two new surfaces widen it.
samples.evidence: editor.ts read-only block: MUTATING_METHODS now includes 'setPageSetup'; api.pasteFormat = () => false
